rounds.proof_sketch: With block_dim=256 and reduction_size=256 (maximum for shape [16,256,256]), each thread processes exactly 1 element at idx=thread_id. The inner loop only completes j=0 before idx≥reduction_size. Whether elements_per_thread is 32 or 31, the outer loop runs once (stride 8192 or 7936 > 256), and inner loop active iterations remain 1.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes elements_per_thread from 32 to 31, which affects the loop stride and iteration count in the optimized kernel. However, for the fixed shape [16, 256, 256], the maximum reduction_size is 256, which equals block_dim (256). In this configuration, each thread independently processes elements at indices thread_id, thread_id+256, thread_id+512, etc. Since reduction_size=256, only index thread_id (< 256) is valid. The change from 32 to 31 iterations in the inner loop is irrelevant because all iterations after j=0 have idx ≥ 256 and are skipped. The outer loop stride change (8192 vs 7936) is also irrelevant since both values exceed reduction_size=256.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation would only be observable if reduction_size > block_dim (256), requiring a reduction dimension > 256 elements. The fixed shape [16, 256, 256] cannot achieve this.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing should include test configurations with larger reduction dimensions (e.g., reduction_size > block_size) to exercise the multi-iteration loop paths in the optimized kernel where elements_per_thread directly affects coverage.
